newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia stocks stay up despite bank sell-off.
newsitem.headline: Australia stocks stay up despite bank sell-off.

text.p: Australian stocks closed slightly higher on Tuesday despite a sell-off in bank shares as investors trod cautiously ahead of the rate-setting Federal Open Markets Committee (FOMC) in the United States later on Tuesday.
The All Ordinaries index closed 1.3 points higher at 2,403.4, about 16 points off its morning high.
Brokers said the market had already factored in a 25 basis point rise in U.S. interest rates and would only react on Wednesday if the move was above or below that.
"It started strongly on the back of the Dow, but fizzled with the banks falling away," said Richard Nelson, a fund manager at BNP Investment Management.
Bank shares boosted the market at the opening but by the end of the day all of the "big four" banks were down.

The turnaround in the bank shares followed an announcement by Treasurer Peter Costello that the government's report into the financial sector would be released in the week starting April 7, brokers said.
The market had been speculating on an imminent release of the report, known as the Wallis Inquiry. The report is widely expected to recommend that rules on bank mergers be loosened.
Despite the bank sell-off, the insurance sector remained buoyant, with the insurance index up over two percent. The Wallis Inquiry also covers the insurance sector.
The market was also weighed down by weaker resource stocks due to a fall in base metal and gold prices.
The share price index futures contract was eight points down at 2,382, creating a 21.4 point discount to the physical index.
